assumptions: Rigid PLA or PETG with a 0.4 mm nozzle and ordinary slicer infill.
A level, firm desk surface is used.

components.form: Flat-extruded pointed arch with shallow convex belly, angular bird/star aperture, and crown star window.
components.interfaces: Only interfaces are the broad fingertip shoulder and continuous desk-contact rocker; there are no mates or assemblies.
components.name: Starling Gate body
components.placement: Print flat on either 82 by 96 mm broad face; use upright on the 82 mm rocker belly.
components.purpose: Carries the silhouette, rocker contact, inertial mass, and dual-reading through-void in one printable solid.

concept.intended_interaction: Place upright on the shallow curved belly and tap one shoulder lightly for an intended tiny three-beat rock, returning to the centered star-window-level pose.
concept.signature_decision: Motion itself performs the bird-to-star reading; no added part, color, text, or decoration carries the trick.
concept.summary: A monolithic rocking arch whose void reads as a perched bird at rest and a shooting-star streak while tilted.
concept.title: Starling Gate
unresolved_risks: Exact tap force, three-beat cadence, and settling time require a physical print and cannot be proven from CAD.
Friction, infill distribution, and first-layer asymmetry can change rocking behavior.

research.evidence_boundary: CAD verification can prove a single positive solid, exact envelope, watertight connected mesh, bed fit, and sampled minimum wall thickness. It cannot prove a physical three-beat cadence, so that remains tuned intent pending physical testing.
research.geometry_basis: The design uses an 82 x 96 x 18 mm one-piece profile, an 18 mm broad load path, 4 mm rocker rise across 82 mm, robust aperture ligaments, and a flat-back print stance.
research.inventor_selection: The complete host roster was compared by declared domain. Pico Press directly covers compact support-free wobble toys with one obvious action and gravity-driven reset; Bob is runner-up but favors multi-part machines, while the remaining optical, deployable, topology, acoustic, game, miniature, and science specialties conflict with the Wish.
